## Problem

Password-reset and invite-registration flows still use the legacy `AuthTokenRepositoryInterface::consumeToken(int $tokenId): void` path after performing their durable mutation. That method updates by token id alone and does not make token type, owner, expiry, and single-winner availability part of the mutation's admission decision.

This was confirmed while independently reviewing #2773. The verified-email correction introduces the predicate-complete `consumeTokenIfAvailable()` contract, but `ResetPasswordController` and invite-mode `RegisterController` remain outside it.

This is a framework token-lifecycle integrity defect. Consumers must not compensate with controller wrappers or application-owned token stores.

Detailed reproduction material remains out of the public issue under `SECURITY.md`; this issue states the remediation contract and non-sensitive acceptance evidence only.

## Required architecture

Define one transactionally coherent spend operation for every single-use auth-token purpose:

- the atomic admission write must bind token id, purpose/type, owning identity (including the deliberate unowned-invite case), unconsumed state, and authoritative expiry;
- the protected durable mutation and token spend must commit or roll back together;
- the operation must have one identity authority and one clock instant for the admission predicate;
- callers must receive an ordinary fail-closed invalid-token result when they lose the single-winner decision;
- `validateToken()` remains descriptive lookup only and must not authorize a later mutation;
- remove the legacy id-only `consumeToken()` path once all production callers migrate.

Do not solve this with an earlier revalidation, a caller-supplied stale timestamp, swallowed persistence errors, or test-only wiring.

## Required behavior

- Password reset changes the password/session generation only when its password-reset token wins the predicate-complete spend in the same transaction.
- A losing, expired, wrong-purpose, wrong-owner, absent, or already-consumed password-reset token cannot mutate credentials.
- Invite registration creates exactly one account per invite-token spend; token admission and user creation/extension rollback are transactionally coherent.
- An unowned invite token matches only the explicit unowned-invite contract, not an arbitrary identity wildcard.
- Existing email-verification single-winner behavior remains intact.
- Token revocation and error handling remain fail closed without exposing token or account existence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inventory every production `validateToken()`, `consumeToken()`, and `consumeTokenIfAvailable()` call site and disposition its transaction boundary.
- [ ] Replace password-reset id-only consumption with a predicate-complete transactional operation.
- [ ] Replace invite-registration id-only consumption with a predicate-complete transactional operation.
- [ ] Remove `consumeToken(int $tokenId): void` from the internal repository contract and implementation when no production caller remains.
- [ ] Tests prove expiry-boundary refusal, wrong type, wrong owner, null-owner semantics, and exactly-one-winner behavior for reset and invite flows.
- [ ] Tests prove losing admission leaves password/session generation and user creation unchanged.
- [ ] Tests prove persistence failure rolls back both the token spend and protected mutation.
- [ ] Production provider/route composition reaches the transactional implementation; mock-only controller tests are insufficient.
- [ ] Upgrade/spec/change records describe the unified token-spend contract.
- [ ] Full Unit, Integration, Architecture, preflight, and changed-line coverage gates pass on the exact candidate SHA.

## Dependency

Discovered during the architecture-integrity review of #2773. It is adjacent to, but predates, the verified-email eligibility defect in #2757.

## Problem

The public verification-resend contract in #2757 uses uniform status/body, bounded lookup, atomic email/IP rate limiting, and uniform exception handling. A synchronous configured mail transport still creates an observable latency difference:

- absent or already-verified accounts return after bounded lookup;
- an active unverified account creates token state, renders mail, and waits for the configured transport (including a SendGrid HTTP request).

A remote caller with repeated samples can statistically distinguish the latter path even though the response envelope is identical. Sleeping or padding in the controller is not a durable fix: provider latency is variable and it would consume request workers.

## Required architecture

Define one durable queued-mail/outbox boundary for public authentication continuations. The HTTP request should perform bounded, constant-shape admission and enqueue work without synchronously contacting the external mail provider. The worker may look up the account, create/replace the token deterministically, and deliver the message without changing the public response.

The design must not make `waaseyaa/auth` depend directly on an optional application queue implementation without a package-layer decision. Prefer a neutral mail-delivery command/outbox contract owned by the appropriate framework package and composed by providers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Absent, verified, and unverified resend requests perform the same request-thread work shape after admission.
- [ ] No external mail transport call occurs before the public response is ready.
- [ ] Enqueued work is durable or fails closed according to a documented production policy.
- [ ] Token replacement remains deterministic and does not produce multiple simultaneously valid verification links.
- [ ] Email/IP limiter behavior and the uniform public response from #2757 are preserved.
- [ ] Worker payloads and logs contain no plaintext verification token beyond the reviewed delivery boundary.
- [ ] Tests measure that the controller does not invoke rendering or transport for any account state and exercise worker delivery separately.

## Confirmed architecture-integrity finding

Part of the FW-ARCH-2026-08 audit. This is the framework blocker discovered while independently reviewing the local #2729 remediation candidate. No implementation, merge, release, or deployment is included here.

**C-22 removed the production `SqlEntityStorage` engine but left the translation API split across two incompatible persistence seams. Normal canonical-repository hydration does not populate an entity's translation bag, while the published translation contract still requires the deleted storage seam.**

This is not merely missing test coverage. It produces incorrect runtime answers on both supported SQL layouts and makes the contract that was supposed to prevent them impossible to execute against production code.

## Exact baseline and measured result

- Commit: `d0d2240dbdb345b64589ed6799b25a0743addb00` (clean `origin/main` before the local #2729 candidate).
- PHP 8.5.9, SQLite, locked dependencies.
- Real `EntitySchemaSync`, `SqlStorageDriver`, and canonical `EntityRepository` composition.
- One entity with real `en` and `fr` translation rows was materialized separately under `sql-blob` and `sql-column`.

| Backend | `find()->getTranslationLanguages()` | `find()->hasTranslation('fr')` | Actual rows via `findTranslations()` |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `sql-blob` | `['en']` | `false` | `['en', 'fr']` |
| `sql-column` | `['en']` | `false` | `['en', 'fr']` |

The same discrepancy reproduces through `InMemoryStorageDriver`; the SQL runs above establish that it is not an in-memory-only artifact.

## Causal path

1. `TranslationController::loadTranslatableEntity()` loads through the canonical `EntityRepositoryInterface::find()` path (`packages/api/src/Controller/TranslationController.php:510-548`). The controller then relies on `getTranslationLanguages()`, `hasTranslation()`, `getTranslation()`, `addTranslation()`, and `removeTranslation()`.
2. `EntityRepository::find()` calls the ordinary private `hydrate()` path (`packages/entity-storage/src/EntityRepository.php:461-496`). That hydrator instantiates the entity but never calls `_setTranslationData()` (`:3187+`).
3. The only live repository call that populates the complete translation map is the separate `findTranslations()` method (`:3129-3176`). Normal API loads do not call it unless the optional `LanguageManager` branch selects a non-default active language.
4. Consequently, stored non-default translations exist but the public translation API reports them missing. `show()` returns a false 404; `index()` omits rows; mutation paths reason from an incomplete bag.
5. The published `Waaseyaa\Entity\Testing\Translation\TranslatableEntityContractTest` cannot catch this. Its abstract factory returns `EntityStorageInterface`, but that interface explicitly says framework SQL repositories do not implement it. A repo-wide search finds no production implementor; only tests/fixtures implement it. Its former SQL engine, `SqlEntityStorage`, was deleted by C-22 WP4.
6. T07 in that contract requires `removeTranslation()` followed by generic `save()` to delete the persisted row, but `_takePendingTranslationDeletions()` has zero production callers. The deletion queue is therefore never drained by either real backend.

The entity-translation specification requires concrete contract subclasses for both SQL backends (FR-060), and the changelog claims `SqlBlobTranslatableContractTest` and `SqlColumnTranslatableContractTest` shipped. Neither class exists.

## Why this blocks #2729

#2729 correctly identifies that production never wires the entity-type authority. Wiring it makes translation methods execute instead of throwing. With the current hydration gap, that converts an obvious failure into incorrect success-shaped negatives: persisted translations are reported absent. The #2729 wiring fix must therefore not land independently of this repair.

## Required architecture decision

Choose one current production authority for translation reads and writes. The preferred direction is the canonical repository introduced by C-22; reviving a second SQL storage engine would recreate the split C-22 was intended to remove.

The design must explicitly settle:

- whether ordinary `find()` returns a translation-complete entity or callers use one clearly named repository operation that does so;
- how `addTranslation()` and `removeTranslation()` become atomic repository writes for both `sql-blob` and `sql-column`;
- where pending translation deletions are consumed, or whether that queue is removed in favor of an explicit repository command;
- whether the obsolete public `EntityStorageInterface` translation test seam is migrated, deprecated, or removed under the stability policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ratify and document one canonical repository-level translation read/write contract; no parallel production storage authority.
- [ ] A normal production route used by `TranslationController` observes every persisted translation without a test-only setter, reflection, raw-row shortcut in the assertion path, or bespoke storage double.
- [ ] `addTranslation()`, updating a translation, and `removeTranslation()` persist atomically through the canonical repository on **both** `sql-blob` and `sql-column`.
- [ ] A failed multi-translation write rolls back all affected rows on both backends.
- [ ] Replace or retarget `TranslatableEntityContractTest` to the surviving production seam and run concrete subclasses against both real SQL backends. An in-memory-only implementor does not satisfy this criterion.
- [ ] Add real-composition API tests proving translation index/show/create/update/delete behavior against stored rows.
- [ ] Remove dead translation persistence code and queues that no production path consumes, or connect them to the canonical implementation and prove the connection.
- [ ] Correct the FR-060/changelog claim so shipped documentation matches executable tests.
- [ ] Re-run #2729's real-kernel authority test on top and prove that wiring the authority no longer exposes false translation negatives.

## Relationships

- Blocks #2729.
- Related to #2055: both are consequences of C-22 deleting `SqlEntityStorage` while leaving public `getStorage()` / `EntityStorageInterface` seams behind. #2055 owns the general dormant-seam/dead-code-gate problem; this issue owns translation correctness and the executable dual-backend contract.

Duplicate checks performed across open and closed issues for `translation hydration`, `findTranslations`, `translation bag`, `pending translation deletions`, `translation write path`, `TranslatableEntityContractTest`, `EntityStorageInterface translation`, `SqlEntityStorage`, and `sql-blob sql-column translation`. #2055 is related but does not own this runtime behavior or acceptance contract.

## Summary

`SqliteArtifactInstaller` provides an in-process atomic swap and exception rollback, but not a crash-recoverable or directory-durable activation protocol. A process or host failure between its two renames can leave the canonical serving path absent; a failure after the second rename but before verification/removal leaves ambiguous state. No startup recovery code interprets the randomized scratch files.

This conflicts with the deployer contract's language about a durable backup and verified atomic activation/restore.

## Evidence

Audit baseline: `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`, Linux/PHP 8.5.9.

A successful installer test passed under `strace` (1 test / 4 assertions). Relevant system calls:

```text
fsync(8) = 0
fsync(6) = 0
rename(".../current.sqlite", ".../.current.sqlite.previous-...") = 0
rename(".../.current.sqlite.install-...", ".../current.sqlite") = 0
```

No containing-directory `fsync` follows backup creation, activation renames, or removal. The implementation has no persisted activation phase/journal and no startup recovery for `.previous-*`, `.install-*`, or `.failed-*` files. Its catch block can restore only if the PHP process survives.

This is deliberately classified as a contract/design gap rather than claiming a simulated power-loss reproduction. The existing normal and injected-exception tests remain valid but do not establish the documented crash boundary.

## Failure windows

- Crash after renaming current to previous but before promoting candidate: canonical database path is absent.
- Crash after promoting candidate but before postflight verification: candidate serves without recorded verification; previous remains ambiguous.
- Crash after unlinking previous but before the directory entry is durable: recovery result depends on filesystem/cache state.
- Backup content can be fsynced while creation of its directory entry remains non-durable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Ratify whether crash/host-power-loss durability is framework-owned or explicitly delegated to a named external deployment transaction owner.
- If framework-owned, define and implement a durable activation state machine with stable transaction identity, directory-entry fsync ordering on supported POSIX filesystems, idempotent startup/resume/rollback, and safe handling of every crash point.
- Prove recovery by terminating the installer at each phase boundary in a child process and invoking the real recovery entrypoint in a new process.
- Preserve and verify the backup, current database, permissions/ownership, WAL quiescence, integrity, and install evidence across retries.
- Explicitly define Windows/non-POSIX support or refusal; do not claim POSIX durability where the runtime cannot provide it.
- Align `packages/deployer/README.md` and `docs/specs/sqlite-artifact-installation.md` with the ratified contract.

## Audit disposition

- Program: FW-ARCH-2026-08
- Workstreams: A5 / A7
- Classification: contract/design gap
- Disposition: **REPLACE** unjournaled two-rename activation, or narrow/delegate the contract through an explicit design decision
- Priority: P1

## Summary

Provider-composed search indexing is a silent best-effort side effect. `SearchIndexSubscriber` catches every index/remove failure, but `SearchServiceProvider` omits the available kernel logger when constructing it, so the subscriber uses `NullLogger`. The same path lazily creates FTS schema on the first post-save write. An incompatible/missing projection shape can therefore run DDL, fail, return the entity save as successful, leave search stale, and emit no operational signal.

Search is derived/rebuildable state, so this is not an argument to roll back canonical content with the index. It is a missing projection-delivery/reconciliation contract and a concrete broken logger wire.

## Reproduction

Audit `FW-ARCH-2026-08`, B05/B07 (A3/A4), PHP 8.5.9.

- frozen `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`
- current-main comparison `6f789ed333aa6c778b76c55f8a6e5338db9769bd`
- real `SearchServiceProvider`, real service resolution, real dispatcher, real FTS indexer/DBAL SQLite, recording kernel logger
- deliberately incompatible existing `search_index` table; real POST_SAVE event carrying an indexable entity
- two frozen runs and one current-main run identical

```json
{
  "save_side_effect_exception_propagated": null,
  "kernel_logger_records": [],
  "search_metadata_exists": true,
  "indexed_rows": 0
}
```

`ensureSchema()` created `search_metadata` during the event, then indexing failed against the incompatible `search_index`. The catch converted failure to save success; the provider-supplied logger observed nothing. The 138-test search suite is green because subscriber failure tests construct it directly and assert only that no exception escapes; provider tests do not inject a failing real index and assert kernel observability/recovery.

## Decision required

Ratify search as a derived projection with one explicit delivery model: synchronous best-effort plus durable dirty marker/reconciliation, transactional outbox/queue, or another bounded mechanism. Canonical entity commit need not wait for search, but a dropped update must be observable and recoverable. Also decide whether projection schema may be created during request/event handling or belongs to deployment/init.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Provider-composed subscriber uses the canonical logger; a real index failure emits structured entity/document/error context.
- [ ] Define stale-projection detection, retry/reconciliation and operator command/metric semantics after post-save/post-delete failure.
- [ ] Decide and enforce schema authority for `search_index` / `search_metadata`; incompatible shape fails diagnostically rather than partial lazy setup plus silent drop.
- [ ] Add real provider→event→index failure/recovery tests, including save, delete and revision-pointer movement.
- [ ] Prove canonical entity success remains explicit and search recovery converges without duplicate/corrupt documents.
- [ ] Qualify separate-search-database and shared-database configurations, repeated workers, interruption and supported platforms.
- [ ] Preserve access-filtered candidate resolution and served-revision re-sourcing.

## Disposition

**KEEP derived search and served-revision projection; REPLACE silent fire-and-forget lifecycle and wire the existing logger immediately within the reviewed design.** Do not make the entity transaction span FTS/network work.

No framework source was changed by this audit.

## Summary

`GroupMembershipService` presents `addMember()` / `assignContent()` as idempotent and says a missing row is created “never a duplicate,” but implements a non-transactional find-then-create with no database uniqueness constraint. Its class-level contract explicitly acknowledges that concurrent calls can create multiple live rows for the same logical membership/content assignment.

This is a known limitation with no open owner, not a newly observed production incident. It is still an architectural contract gap: `docs/specs/relationship-modeling.md` requires duplicate-edge policy to be explicit—unique constraint or idempotent upsert—and the current path is neither concurrency-safe uniqueness nor an explicitly duplicate-permitted model.

## Evidence

Audit `FW-ARCH-2026-08`, B01/B07 (A2/A4).

- frozen `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`
- current-main comparison `6f789ed333aa6c778b76c55f8a6e5338db9769bd`
- groups tree identical at both: `03d8ae937b52fe4eb59a2ef736c4d2e976ada743`
- PHP 8.5.9; groups suite 86 tests / 739 assertions, exit 0

`findExistingRelationshipId()` performs an access-disabled query and then `upsertLiveRelationship()` separately creates/saves. `RelationshipSchemaManager` requires fields only; no unique key protects `(relationship_type, from_entity_type, from_entity_id, to_entity_type, to_entity_id)` or the group-specific subset. The revoke path deliberately finds and revokes all duplicates, proving duplicate rows are accepted state rather than prevented state.

The generic relationship model may legitimately allow multiple edges with the same endpoints (temporal/source semantics), so a blanket global unique constraint is not assumed safe. The decision may need relationship-type-specific identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ratify logical identity and duplicate policy for `group_membership` and `group_content`, including soft-revoked rows and reactivation.
- [ ] Choose an atomic supported-backend enforcement mechanism (type-specific unique key/claim, transactional upsert, or another explicit authority) without banning valid duplicate semantics for unrelated relationship types.
- [ ] Add two-connection concurrency tests for create/create and create/reactivate races on both first-party SQL layouts.
- [ ] Define cleanup/migration for pre-existing duplicate live and revoked rows; no silent arbitrary winner.
- [ ] Preserve duplicate-tolerant revoke behavior during migration and prove audit/history expectations.
- [ ] Align method/class documentation so “idempotent” has one concurrency meaning.

## Disposition

**DEFER pending design, then REPLACE the check-then-create path for these relationship types.** Keep the generic relationship model and duplicate-tolerant revoke until compatibility and cleanup are settled.

No framework source was changed by this audit.

## Summary

Media has two upload-policy/configuration authorities. `MediaServiceProvider` binds an `UploadHandler` from nested `media.upload_path`, `media.allowed_types`, and `media.max_size`, but the provider-composed `MediaRouter` does not resolve or inject that binding. The live router constructs a new handler and reads top-level `files_*`, `upload_max_bytes`, and `upload_allowed_mime_types` with different defaults.

The provider binding is therefore a success-shaped dead path: consumers can resolve and test one configured policy while HTTP enforces another.

## Evidence

Audit `FW-ARCH-2026-08`, B07/A4. Frozen `50750231a…`, current-main `6f789ed333…`, identical media tree `22dc4fad56a6d1492c72761ac3b4c59972368e1d`, PHP 8.5.9. Two frozen runs and one current-main run were identical.

With the same config containing nested `media.max_size = 1` and `media.allowed_types = [text/plain]`:

```json
{
  "provider_bound_handler_validation_errors": ["File must be under 0MB."],
  "live_router_max_bytes_from_same_config": 10485760,
  "live_router_allowed_types_from_same_config": [
    "image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/gif", "image/webp", "application/pdf", "text/plain"
  ]
}
```

The provider creates `MediaRouter` without its `UploadHandler` argument. `MediaRouter` then constructs its own handler. The bound handler's defaults are 5 MiB/images; the router's defaults are 10 MiB plus PDF/text. Package tests exercise each class independently, so 210 tests remain green.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ratify one upload policy/config schema and compatibility precedence for existing top-level and nested keys.
- [ ] Make the provider-composed HTTP route consume that one authority; no second handler construction with divergent defaults.
- [ ] Decide whether the public provider binding remains supported or is removed with an upgrade note.
- [ ] Add a provider-to-router real-composition test showing configured size and MIME decisions, including invalid/missing config.
- [ ] Keep sniff-only MIME enforcement and bundle/create authorization unchanged.
- [ ] Remove the dead configuration path after migration; do not retain dual reads indefinitely without an explicit deprecation window.

## Disposition

**CONSOLIDATE / REPLACE dual authority.** Needs a compatibility decision before implementation because both key families and the public `UploadHandler` binding may have downstream users.

No framework source was changed by this audit.

## Summary

The engagement package allows any authenticated caller to persist a reaction, comment, or follow whose `target_type` is unknown or whose `target_id` does not exist. `save(..., validate: true)` accepts the row. The same package then deliberately denies every read because the parent cannot be resolved.

This is a contract gap rather than a claim that the current documented behavior is violated: the README promises authenticated-only creation and fail-closed parent-cascaded reads, and the implementation does exactly that. The missing decision is whether durable engagement is allowed to be born unreachable, and where polymorphic-reference integrity belongs.

## Evidence

Audit: `FW-ARCH-2026-08`, boundary B07 / A4 with A2.

- frozen source: `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`
- current-main comparison: `6f789ed333aa6c778b76c55f8a6e5338db9769bd`
- `packages/engagement` tree object is byte-identical at both heads: `70a08ac949ee63c13b4b16173ccf6c5f5b1de074`
- PHP 8.5.9, real SQLite `SqlStorageDriver`, real `EntityRepository`, `validate: true`, real `EngagementAccessPolicy`
- two frozen runs plus one current-main run were identical

Observed:

```json
{
  "create_access_allowed": true,
  "target_type_field_edit_forbidden": false,
  "target_id_field_edit_forbidden": false,
  "save_validate_true_threw": null,
  "persisted_id": 1,
  "reloaded": true,
  "view_allowed": false
}
```

The constructors require the two target fields but do not validate them. They are ordinary string/integer fields, not one declared entity-reference contract. `createAccess()` checks authentication only; `fieldAccess()` protects only `user_id`; repository validation derives no existence/access constraint; `viewAccess()` is the first place that resolves the parent and fails closed.

## Decision required

Choose and document one authority:

1. creation validates target existence and caller access at the canonical mutation boundary;
2. unresolved targets are intentionally permitted (for eventual/imported references), with an explicit lifecycle, observability and cleanup contract; or
3. engagement owns a different durable reference representation that can enforce the chosen invariant.

Do not fix this only in an HTTP controller: importers, jobs, tools and direct repository callers would retain the gap. Do not add a database FK without addressing polymorphic target types and both first-party storage layouts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ratify whether a newly persisted engagement may reference an unknown type, missing row, or parent the actor cannot view.
- [ ] Name the mutation/reference authority and supported eventual/import lifecycle, if any.
- [ ] Apply the decision consistently to reaction, comment and follow across generic HTTP create/update, repository callers, jobs/tools/imports, and both `sql-blob` and `sql-column` layouts.
- [ ] Add real-composition positive and negative tests: visible existing parent, missing type, missing ID, hidden parent, and parent removed after creation.
- [ ] Define deletion/retention behavior for engagement whose parent later disappears.
- [ ] Document compatibility and cleanup for existing unresolved rows before enforcing a stricter rule.

## Disposition

**DEFER pending design; KEEP the fail-closed read policy.** If creation-time integrity is selected, replace the split unvalidated write path with one canonical reference/mutation rule and retire adapter-specific checks rather than layering more fallbacks.

No framework implementation was changed by this audit finding.

## Summary

> **Terminology correction (audit follow-up):** `InMemoryStorageDriver` is the first-party testing driver, not one of the production field-storage backends (`sql-blob` / `sql-column`). The production defect below is the non-atomic SQL path. The in-memory result proves the framework's test composition cannot model messaging faithfully; it is not evidence of a second production backend outage.

Messaging's creator membership is implemented as a best-effort POST_SAVE side effect even though it is the required invariant that makes a thread usable. The production SQL path is non-atomic, and the first-party in-memory test composition cannot model it:

- **First-party in-memory testing driver:** bootstrap always fails because its dedupe calls `EntityRepository::getQuery()` without a database; the exception is swallowed. `MessagingAccessPolicy` uses the same SQL-only query, so even a manually seeded participant cannot access the thread. This makes the test backend an invalid substitute for this package.
- **SQL:** any participant INSERT failure is swallowed after the thread commits, leaving an orphaned thread that its creator cannot view or post to.

## Invariant

A successful authenticated `message_thread` creation must leave exactly one owner membership for the acting creator, and the access authority must recognize it on every supported backend. If the membership cannot be established, thread creation must not report success or leave an inaccessible durable row.

## Evidence

Frozen audit baseline `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`, clean, PHP 8.5.9. Current main `6f789ed333aa6c778b76c55f8a6e5338db9769bd` has no messaging changes.

Two controlled runs were identical:

```json
{
  "memory_success_participants": 0,
  "memory_bootstrap_error": "EntityRepository for thread_participant was constructed without a database; getQuery() requires one.",
  "memory_participants_after_manual_seed": 1,
  "memory_creator_can_view_after_manual_seed": false,
  "sql_failure_was_propagated": null,
  "sql_thread_rows_after_participant_failure": 1,
  "sql_participant_rows_after_failure": 0,
  "creator_can_view_orphaned_thread": false
}
```

The SQL failure was injected with a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `thread_participant`; no fake repository was involved. The in-memory path used `InMemoryStorageDriver` through `V2EntityRepositoryFactory`.

All five entity-package suites are green (243 tests / 469 assertions). Messaging's "end-to-end" bootstrap test builds only a SQLite manager and exercises only successful insertion. No test crosses the failure boundary or runs the complete lifecycle on the in-memory backend.

This follows closed #1915: that issue correctly identified the original bootstrap deadlock, but the fix classified mandatory membership as a best-effort side effect.

## Disposition

**REWRITE**, not a catch tweak. Move creator membership into the authoritative thread-creation transaction/use case and give policies a backend-capable membership lookup. Do not preserve an inaccessible thread as graceful degradation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ratify the thread-creation authority and transaction boundary; creator membership is part of its success contract.
- [ ] Authenticated thread creation either persists thread + exactly one owner together or persists neither.
- [ ] Participant insertion failure is surfaced and does not leave an inaccessible thread.
- [ ] Membership lookup works in production SQL composition and in the framework's in-memory test composition, or the in-memory composition explicitly refuses unsupported packages before tests can mistake it for parity.
- [ ] A manually present membership is recognized by access policy in every supported composition named above.
- [ ] Verify the package's declared `sql-blob` schema transition; do not imply `sql-column` support unless the entity definitions are deliberately widened to it.
- [ ] Concurrent/retried creation cannot create duplicate owner memberships.
- [ ] Canonical `MessagingServiceProvider` boot is exercised, rather than registering the subscriber directly in every test.
- [ ] Failure-injection covers production SQL; success/parity coverage includes the in-memory testing driver under its ratified support contract.

## Audit linkage

- Architecture umbrella: #2723
- A4 runtime/effectiveness: #2724
- A7 root-cause synthesis: #2727
- Original remediation: #1915
- Related transaction-boundary concern: #2734

## Summary

`waaseyaa/analytics` and `waaseyaa/github` each implement a private PHP-stream HTTP stack instead of using the shared `waaseyaa/http-client` authority created by #644. The duplicated transports have already drifted into observably wrong runtime behavior while their package tests stay green.

This is one adoption/authority finding, not a request to merge two domain APIs.

## Evidence

Frozen baseline `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`, clean, PHP 8.5.9. Current main `6f789ed333aa6c778b76c55f8a6e5338db9769bd` has no changes in either package.

### Analytics false success

`StreamTransport` sets `ignore_errors=true` but returns only `string|false`. `UmamiClient` treats a non-empty HTTP error body as success. A controlled server returned HTTP 500 with JSON; no failure was logged:

```json
{"server_status":500,"failure_log_count":0,"failure_was_reported":false}
```

### GitHub unbounded request

`GitHubClient::request()` sets no timeout. A controlled server accepted the connection and stalled; PHP remained blocked until an external two-second timeout killed the probe (`exit 124`). The client also discards response headers, so its `listIssues()` / `listMilestones()` API has no pagination mechanism.

Two runs produced the same outcomes. The combined package suites remain green: 29 tests / 85 assertions. Analytics tests inject a fake transport; GitHub tests override `request()` completely, so neither tests its default transport semantics.

By contrast, `StreamHttpClient` already supplies status-bearing responses, explicit timeout, response-size bound, scheme validation, redirect refusal, TLS policy, and header-injection guards.

## Disposition

**KEEP** the Umami and GitHub domain façades. **REPLACE** their duplicated stream implementations with the shared HTTP transport authority, or ratify and enforce a documented exception if analytics must remain dependency-free.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ratify `waaseyaa/http-client` as the single default outbound HTTP authority, including the policy for Layer-0/zero-dependency packages.
- [ ] Analytics distinguishes HTTP failure status from success and exercises the default adapter against a real local server.
- [ ] GitHub requests have an explicit timeout/body bound and use an injectable client rather than test-only method overriding.
- [ ] GitHub list APIs either follow pagination deterministically or state and expose their single-page contract.
- [ ] Package tests cover default adapter status, timeout, malformed JSON, and transport failures without external network access.
- [ ] Remove the duplicate raw stream code once adoption is complete.

## Summary

`waaseyaa/billing`'s webhook idempotency seam acknowledges a Stripe event before the caller can persist the payment/subscription effect. A downstream failure therefore turns Stripe's retry into `null` and permanently loses the event. The canonical service-provider binding has the opposite failure mode: it never injects the claim callback, so duplicate deliveries both pass through.

The package is explicitly deferred scaffolding, so this is a **pre-activation architecture contract** rather than a claim that billing is production-enabled today.

## Invariant

An external delivery may be acknowledged as complete only with the durable business effect, or via an inbox state machine that can safely resume after failure. Duplicate suppression must not convert a recoverable processing failure into data loss.

## Evidence

Frozen audit baseline: `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`, clean, PHP 8.5.9. Current main comparison `6f789ed333aa6c778b76c55f8a6e5338db9769bd` is unchanged and reproduces.

`WebhookHandler::handle()` calls `$claimEvent($eventId)` and only then returns normalized data. The caller necessarily performs its durable effect after that return. Failure injection produced:

```json
{
  "claim_is_consumed_before_downstream_effect": true,
  "retry_after_downstream_failure": null,
  "downstream_effect_count_after_retry": 0,
  "canonical_provider_first_delivery": "evt_audit_once",
  "canonical_provider_duplicate_delivery": "evt_audit_once"
}
```

Two probe runs were byte-identical. The package suite is green (37 tests, 81 assertions) because the idempotency test stops at handler return and does not model downstream failure.

`BillingServiceProvider` constructs `WebhookHandler` without the optional claim callback, so its canonical binding cannot satisfy the README's instruction that production consumers provide a durable atomic claim.

The seam was introduced in `8f0721115` / #2010 as hardening; this issue tracks the remaining boundary defect without reopening that multi-package anchor.

## Disposition

**Replace before activation.** Keep billing deferred until the processing/acknowledgement authority is explicit and tested end to end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ratify a single ownership model: framework-owned durable inbox/processor, or a mapper-only handler with idempotency owned explicitly by the consumer.
- [ ] A crash/failure after receive but before durable business effect does not suppress a later retry.
- [ ] Concurrent deliveries of one Stripe event produce one completed business effect.
- [ ] Completion acknowledgement is transactional with the business effect, or recoverable processing/lease states are proven.
- [ ] `BillingServiceProvider` exposes the ratified production composition; it does not silently bind a duplicate-permitting handler.
- [ ] Integration tests cover canonical provider wiring, duplicate concurrency, downstream failure, and successful retry.
- [ ] Align `StripeClientInterface` documentation: README calls it public/downstream-facing while source marks it `@internal`.

## Confirmed finding: B06-BROADCAST-01

FW-ARCH-2026-08; assessment #2724, synthesis #2727. **P1 / Needs Design.** `BroadcastStorage::pushRetained()` can report failure after the live message is already committed, and a normal retry duplicates the live event.

### Reproduction

Use real DBAL SQLite, the shipped broadcast schema and both real Wayfinding callers. Install a SQLite trigger that refuses inserts into `_broadcast_retained`:

- HTTP throws and the MCP tool returns `emit failed`.
- After the reported failure, `_broadcast_log` has one pollable row while `_broadcast_retained` is empty.
- Remove the fault and retry the identical operation: both callers report success, with two live log rows and one retained row.

Reproduced twice with byte-identical results. The live side effect is externally observable by an active SSE subscriber; this is not just stale internal bookkeeping.

### Root cause

`pushRetained()` documents one operation that pushes and retains the same message/id, but executes log INSERT, retained DELETE and retained INSERT without a transaction. Any failure after the first statement violates that combined-operation contract. The adapters' different error envelopes do not change the shared partial effect.

Open-and-closed issue search found no owner for `pushRetained`, retained broadcast atomicity or retry duplication.

### Design and acceptance

- Make live-log insertion and retained last-write-wins replacement atomic on supported SQLite and MySQL backends while preserving the shared `msg_id`, TTL and replay de-duplication contract.
- Define behavior when called inside an already-open transaction; coordinate with #2734 rather than introducing an independent nested-transaction fiction.
- Prove rollback at every statement boundary, including an existing retained row: on failure, neither the old retained state nor the live log may be partially changed.
- Prove retry, same-key replacement, different keys, expiry, poll/replay identity and concurrent-writer behavior on both supported backends.
- Keep failure visible to callers. Do not catch and report success, delete the committed log as compensation after it may have been observed, or patch only Wayfinding.
- Inventory all `pushRetained()` callers and public compatibility; independent review required.

Evidence: frozen clean source `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`, PHP 8.5.9. Relevant production files are unchanged on checked main snapshot `6f789ed333aa6c778b76c55f8a6e5338db9769bd`.

No implementation is authorized by this audit finding. Local report: `outputs/FW-ARCH-2026-08-B06/REPORT.md`; portable publication remains pending.

## Confirmed finding: A3-NOTIFY-01

FW-ARCH-2026-08; assessment #2723, synthesis #2727. **P1 / Needs Design.** Persistent async notification delivery does not preserve mail recipient routing.

### Reproduction

Use real NotificationServiceProvider + MailServiceProvider + QueueServiceProvider, shipped queue/notification schema, DbalQueue/DbalTransport/Worker, signed authority envelope, DatabaseChannel, MailChannel/Mailer and ArrayTransport. Original DefaultNotifiable routes `mail` to `recipient@example.test`; notification's `toMail()` asks the recipient for that route.

- Synchronous `send()` delivers the correct mail and writes one notification row.
- `sendAsync()` with SyncQueue does the same.
- Persistent `sendAsync()` serializes and replays the real notification but mail receives null and Envelope construction throws a TypeError. After three tries: no mail, one failed-job row, no queue row. The database channel ran before mail and inserted on each attempt.
- Counterexample: an otherwise identical notification whose renderer uses a fixed synthetic address crosses the persistent queue and real MailChannel successfully. This isolates recipient reconstruction, not notification serialization or mail transport.

Two fresh runs reproduce. Separate #1578 owns repeated earlier-channel effects; this issue owns lost recipient routing.

### Root cause

SendNotificationJob persists only notifiable type and ID. SendNotificationHandler::buildNotifiable() returns an anonymous NotifiableInterface whose `routeNotificationFor()` supports only `database`; all other channels return null. It presents a general interface while lacking the original route data/resolution authority. Existing async tests inspect that `toMail()` survived serialization but use a recording channel and never execute its recipient route.

### Evidence boundaries

Frozen source `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`, sealed ZIP consumer lock SHA256 `b4ecb5fd9fcd7d96b989f50b5b251caf52a64e8b43950f7ede5d755998aec396`, PHP 8.5.9. Nine cases repeated: 9 controls pass, 3 negative predicates fail per run. Installed bytes reverified; notification/mail source unchanged at main `1f69359204c9d572b85da7a4c907d0c6cff4903a`. Probe exits 1; stderr empty. No full-main dependency or suite claim.

Provider service boundaries are real; authority resolver/epoch are fixtures. Mail uses local ArrayTransport/LocalTransport only, no network. Not full kernel, real SMTP/SendGrid, concurrency or HTTP qualification.

### Design and acceptance

- Choose the owner of async recipient routing: a reviewed immutable per-channel route snapshot or authoritative notifiable resolution at execution. Define privacy, address changes, deletion, tenant/type resolution, external implementors and payload compatibility first.
- Retire the anonymous pseudo-notifiable path that only knows database routing. Do not hardcode `email`, silently drop mail, use an unconditional fallback address, or serialize arbitrary live entity graphs.
- Prove synchronous and persistent async parity through real MailChannel, signing/envelope, serialize, DB transport and Worker. Include database and mail, unknown/missing route, changed/deleted recipient, failure/retry and custom notifiable controls.
- Preserve exact notification renderer behavior, queue authority, failure reporting and SyncQueue behavior. Coordinate duplicate-channel disposition with #1578 and channel availability with #1624; do not duplicate them here.
- Inventory public NotifiableInterface/NotificationInterface consumers and existing queued SendNotificationJob payloads; document migration/breaking-change policy. Independent review required.

No implementation is authorized by this audit finding. Local full report: `outputs/FW-ARCH-2026-08-A3-notification-delivery/REPORT.md`. Portable publication remains pending.

## FW-ARCH-2026-08: A3-QUEUE-03 / related A3-QUEUE-04

Assessment #2723; synthesis #2727. **P1 / Needs Design.** One bounded owner for durable queue-to-failed-store handoff recovery. Not a whole queue rewrite, not authorization to implement, and not a duplicate of #2741's active-delivery settlement contract.

### Confirmed recovery defect: A3-QUEUE-03

The live claim exclusion added under #2010 works, but `DatabaseFailedJobRepository::claimForRetry()` stores only a non-null `retried_at` marker. QueueRetryHandler and QueueController then enqueue and forget in separate operations.

Both actual CLI handler and API controller reproduce:

1. Child process claims a real failed job, then terminates before enqueue: failed row remains, queue is empty. Subsequent retries return CLI exit 1 / API 409. Backdating the marker to year 2000 does not change this. No retry process is still running.
2. Child terminates after successful enqueue but before failed-row deletion: one queued copy exists. Repeated retry correctly does not duplicate it, but even after the worker successfully executes that copy the failed row remains claimed and returns the same conflict.

The payload is not physically lost; a developer can call low-level releaseRetryClaim. The defect is a stranded normal retry workflow with no safe durable outcome/reconciliation. Blindly clearing old markers is not sufficient: it would confuse an unperformed retry with a replay that already completed.

### Related measured behavior / contract decision: A3-QUEUE-04

Terminate Worker after the real failed-record INSERT but before queue rejection. Recovery reclaims the original exhausted queue row, correctly refuses another handler execution, but inserts a second independently retryable failed record. Retrying both records through QueueController returns 204 twice and produces two queue rows with identical payload digests.

This is a confirmed interruption outcome, **not an assertion of a promised exactly-once guarantee**. Decide whether failure-record/transfer identity must be idempotent or duplicates are an explicit bounded operator-visible policy. Write-before-delete alone does not answer it. Do not deduplicate all messages by payload hash: identical legitimate jobs may be separate deliveries.

### Evidence

- Frozen source `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`, PHP 8.5.9, independently installed sealed ZIP consumer; lock SHA256 `b4ecb5fd9fcd7d96b989f50b5b251caf52a64e8b43950f7ede5d755998aec396`.
- 13 cases repeated on fresh SQLite files: **17 control predicates pass, 5 recovery/contract predicates fail per run**. Probe exits 1 with complete output and separate metadata; all ten deliberate child exits are 73. Stderr empty. Installed artifacts reverified and PHP helpers lint cleanly.
- Queue package plus CLI retry handler and API queue controller are unchanged at main snapshot `1f69359204c9d572b85da7a4c907d0c6cff4903a`; this is source parity, not a fresh full-main suite pass.
- Real provider-built queue/transport/repository, actual failed-job seeding and signed replay. Real handler/controller service boundaries; no CLI parser or HTTP middleware qualification. Authority resolver and epoch are fixtures. Fault-only repository decorator delegates storage then exits a child at the exact selected seam. This is not SIGKILL/OOM/power-loss evidence.
- Scratch timestamps are explicitly aged; no actual clock waits. Entity sql-blob/sql-column layouts are irrelevant to these queue tables.

Passing controls include live two-connection claim exclusion, explicit owner release, exact payload/original queue replay and subsequent successful execution, corrupt payload retention (CLI 1/API 422), dispatch failure claim release (CLI 1/API 502) and successful recovery, no duplicate after enqueue interruption, and no re-execution of exhausted work.

### Bounded design / retirement acceptance

- Define delivery/retry identity, claim ownership lifetime, transfer outcome and safe operator reconciliation. Choose same-database atomic capability and/or durable idempotent transfer semantics; do not imply atomicity across unrelated transports/connections.
- Retire timestamp-only retry recovery and independent adapter-owned claim/enqueue/forget orchestration in favor of the chosen framework-owned transition. Preserve adapter-specific output/status behavior.
- Explicitly disposition Worker record/reject interruption; preserve attempt-budget behavior and original failure evidence without silently creating unlimited indistinguishable retry authorities.
- Preserve authenticated exact-byte replay, original queue name, live contention exclusion, corrupt-row retention and caught-outage recovery. No unconditional claim expiry/reset, swallowed exceptions, unsigned fallback or gate weakening.
- Prove each interruption before/after on persistent storage, both CLI/API service paths, current-owner exclusion and completed-replay reconciliation. Test recovery repeatedly, including work already consumed before reconciliation. Do not keep a database transaction open around arbitrary Job::handle().
- Inventory public FailedJobRepositoryInterface/TransportInterface consumers; document old failed/reserved rows, mixed-version workers, external transports and compatibility/migration policy before implementation.
- Coordinate with #2741's claim receipt design where types overlap, without conflating active delivery and failed-row retry ownership. #2734 remains separate. No mandatory dependency on their merges unless the chosen design actually needs it.
- Independent review of the contract and exact-head evidence before landing. If implementation is split, derive small candidates from this one transition contract, not independent CLI/API workarounds.

### Existing ownership and publication

Reviewed closed #1915 (API forget-before-dispatch) and #2010 (atomic live retry claim), plus open/closed interruption/retry searches and repository call sites. Their original protections still pass; this is their unhandled process-interruption lifecycle, not evidence those fixes did nothing. No matching dedicated recovery issue found.

Full local report/probe/logs: `outputs/FW-ARCH-2026-08-A3-queue-recovery/REPORT.md`. Hashes are bound in per-run exit records. Repository-portable publication and independent review remain outstanding; neither this issue nor these probes close A3/A7.

## Confirmed finding: A3-QUEUE-02

FW-ARCH-2026-08; assessment owner #2723, synthesis #2727, parent #2719. Priority P1: an obsolete worker can delete a live delivery or release it for another concurrent execution. This is distinct from repository/scheduler outer-commit ownership in #2734.

### Evidence and limits

Runtime: frozen audit source `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f`, independently installed sealed ZIP packages, PHP 8.5.9, SQLite through real DBAL connections. Consumer lock SHA256 `b4ecb5fd9fcd7d96b989f50b5b251caf52a64e8b43950f7ede5d755998aec396`. Installed archive bytes reverified. The entire `packages/queue` tree is unchanged at current-main snapshot `1f69359204c9d572b85da7a4c907d0c6cff4903a`; this is a source comparison, not a full current-main runtime qualification.

Two fresh runs reproduce all four stale-settlement cases. Each uses two independent connections to the same disposable SQLite file, the shipped queue migration, a real provider-built DbalQueue/DbalTransport and a signed, enveloped Job. Claims and settlement use real transports; this is not two running worker processes. Only the fixture reservation timestamp is explicitly aged to model an elapsed visibility window. No real crash, wall-clock timing, power-loss or simultaneous contention guarantee is claimed.

1. A pops a job; B cannot pop while A's claim is live (passing control).
2. Set that fixture row's `reserved_at` to `time()-1000`; B pops the same job, with attempts incremented from 0 to 1 (passing control).
3. A settles using the ID returned by its obsolete claim.

| Obsolete A operation | Observed effect on B's current claim |
|---|---|
| ack | Row deleted |
| reject | Row deleted |
| release | Reservation cleared, attempts 1 -> 2 |
| defer | Reservation cleared, attempts remains 1 |

The negative oracle is that B's queued row/claim should remain unchanged by an obsolete A receipt. All four predicates fail, twice. At-least-once delivery permits duplicate execution; it does not by itself settle the design question of allowing obsolete owners to mutate a newer claim. Record and review that contract explicitly.

### Root cause / authority

`packages/queue/src/Transport/DbalTransport.php::pop()` conditionally claims/reclaims a row but returns only id/payload/attempts. `ack()`, `reject()`, `release()` and `defer()` identify the target solely by row ID. `TransportInterface` cannot express which reservation a settlement belongs to. Worker passes those IDs directly. Atomic acquisition does not establish ownership of subsequent settlement.

The existing `DbalTransportTest` and real-transport `CrashRecoveryTest` cover expiry/reclaim and retry exhaustion, but do not return the obsolete worker after reclaim. `AbstractTransportContract` covers listing, release counting and defer counting, not stale-owner settlement. These tests are useful and should remain.

### Bounded remediation / design gate

Owning implementation boundary: queue transport reservation contract; consumers: Worker, both first-party transports and external TransportInterface implementors.

- Decide and document a per-claim receipt/generation contract, including stale-settlement outcomes and expiry policy. A row ID or second-resolution timestamp alone is not a unique claim receipt.
- Replace worker-side ID-only settlement with ownership-checked settlement. Do not retain a silent unsafe fallback for legacy worker callers; separate any intentional administrator force-delete operation from delivery completion authority.
- Inventory every transport implementation/caller and publish an API compatibility/migration decision before changing the interface. Adapt the in-memory transport contract as well; queue delivery is independent of entity sql-blob/sql-column layouts.
- Test two connections: live claim exclusion; expiry/reclaim; stale ack/reject/release/defer preserving B; B settling successfully; repeated handoffs; same-clock-tick claim distinction. Add a composed Worker case, not only low-level transport cases.
- Preserve retry counting, delays, failed-record-before-delete ordering and existing occurrence/runtime-epoch behavior. Explicitly decide how stale workers' failed-record writes are handled; guarding DELETE alone must not be described as fencing all effects.
- Define upgrade behavior for queued/reserved rows and mixed old/new workers; do not imply exactly-once business effects.
- Independent review must verify the receipt flows through real provider composition and that the ID-only worker path is retired, without weakening gates.

Dependencies: contract decision -> implementation and first-party consumer migration -> compatibility/upgrade evidence -> independent review. No dependency on #2734's code fix; shared A7 authority-lifetime cluster only. Implementation is not authorized by this finding.

### Duplicate/history review

Searched open and closed issues for queue claim/lease/visibility/stale ack/DbalTransport, and repository audit/CL records. #516 is a closed durable-queue design predecessor; #2010's atomic claim concerns failed-job retry admission, not active-delivery settlement. #2488's queue-vs-Messenger discussion is not this defect. No matching concrete remediation owner found.

Full local evidence bundle: `outputs/FW-ARCH-2026-08-A3-queue-delivery/` (probe SHA256 `23c7d7656bc4f2417b9ce3b3e9e82a629d729c8a2445c45bd636c461f408eef1`). Separate command exits and full stdout/stderr retained. Repository-portable publication and independent review remain outstanding; this issue does not close A3.

## Follow-up from #2728 — delete-refusal surface

> **Correction history.** The first version incorrectly said the baseline returned 204 and #2728 introduced new 500s. The 2026-08-30 correction established that the guard already threw. A further boundary check qualifies the data outcome: **unfenced** refusal changes from error+deleted to error+preserved; **DatabaseFenceGuard on the same connection** preserves the entity on both versions. The earlier claim that every caller catches only EntityMutationConflictException was also incorrect: PurgeJob catches Throwable per policy. These corrections do not change this issue's remediation scope.

`RelationshipDeleteGuardListener` refuses with a bare `\RuntimeException` (`packages/relationship/src/RelationshipDeleteGuardListener.php`). The API's `EntityMutationConflictException` mapping does not handle that refusal, so it can surface as HTTP 500 rather than a typed conflict response. The untyped refusal also prevents callers from reliably distinguishing an integrity refusal from an infrastructure fault.

**This error shape is pre-existing, not introduced by #2728.** The old `UnitOfWork` buffered-dispatch drain ran outside its rollback catch. Without an outer transaction the guard threw after durable deletion; inside `DatabaseFenceGuard`, the unit's commit only released a savepoint, and the propagated exception rolled back the outer transaction.

| Execution context | Before #2728 | After #2728 |
|---|---|---|
| API / GraphQL / tool repository delete without an outer transaction | error, row deleted | error, row preserved |
| PurgeJob without a lease or another outer transaction | policy failure, entity purged | policy failure, entity retained |
| PurgeJob effect inside DatabaseFenceGuard on the same connection | policy failure, entity retained by outer rollback | policy failure, entity retained |

### Retention and policy failure

Retention is newly effective for an **unfenced** guard refusal. It is pre-existing for fenced execution. Since the relationship contract deliberately rejects automatic cascade deletion, a linked entity can remain past its retention deadline until its relationships are removed or repointed. The operator-visible handling remains necessary regardless of which version first retained it.

`PurgeJob::run()` catches `\Throwable` per policy, logs `classification.retention.purge_failed` and proceeds to the next policy; remaining entities of the failed policy are skipped. `LeaseLostException` is rethrown. This is not a per-entity catch and not an HTTP error surface.

### Scope (unchanged)

- Give the guard a typed exception so an integrity refusal is distinguishable from infrastructure failure.
- Map it to a clean HTTP/GraphQL/tool refusal, following the existing conflict-mapping precedent.
- Decide the retention story for permanently blocked entities: per-entity isolation in PurgeJob, an operator-visible report, or an explicit policy.
- Do not swallow the refusal or reinstate orphaning.
- Keep the existing outer-transaction/post-commit-effect defect in #2734 separate.

### Evidence boundary

Source inspected: PurgeJob, UnitOfWork, RelationshipDeleteGuardListener and DatabaseFenceGuard. The real EntityTypeManagerFactory + relationship guard + database-fence composition was executed on baseline `50750231a8036ae7afc68416fed8ea271e47159f` and #2735 production source `18c44011bb5ed9b23653c4589ce16c0ff67dd6b4`, both unfenced and fenced, on Windows/PHP8.5.5 and WSL/PHP8.5.9: eight cases matched the table's persistence boundary. This is **not** a full PurgeJob sweep test; its catch/continuation behavior is established here by source inspection. No refusal-surface implementation has been made by this correction.

Related upgrade note: `docs/upgrade-notes/pre-delete-event-timing.md`; the matching documentation patch is handed off on #2735.

## Confirmed defect

StreamHttpClient reads at most maxResponseBytes with stream_get_contents, then closes the stream and returns the string unless it is false. Reaching the size ceiling is not distinguished from a complete response. A caller can receive HTTP 200 with a partial file and no exception.

Source inspected on main at 7cc9dfcba18ba122033161488a450624af242202: packages/http-client/src/StreamHttpClient.php, fetch(), approximately lines 139–157. The same path is present in the GoFormX control-plane lock at framework 0.1.0-alpha.299.

## Runnable evidence

Using native PHP 8.5.5 and the locked framework client against a disposable loopback Node HTTP server:

1. Server returns HTTP 200, Content-Length: 100, and a complete 100-byte synthetic body.
2. Client uses new StreamHttpClient(timeout: 2.0, maxResponseBytes: 8).
3. get() returns normally: status=200, declaredBytes=100, receivedBytes=8, exception=false.

No live credentials, production data, or external service was involved. Current-main source matches the defect path; the runtime probe used the installed release, not a separate execution of main.

## Impact and priority

P1 data-integrity/reliability issue for callers consuming downloads, CSV, or other bodies without their own completeness check. It does not establish a confidentiality exploit. JSON consumers may instead see downstream parse failures. Merely bounding memory must not silently redefine a successful complete response as its prefix.

GoFormX PR goformx/goformx#153 adds explicit export Content-Length, and the in-progress control-plane proxy compares declared length with the fully buffered body before offering an attachment. That is an application-level mitigation, not a generic framework fix.

## Acceptance

- Reject over-limit responses with a typed transport failure; no partial HttpResponse success.
- Distinguish an exactly-at-limit complete body from a body exceeding the limit (including chunked/unknown-length responses), while keeping memory bounded.

- Preserve TLS verification, no redirect following, header-injection defense, and bounded connection/read behavior.
- Do not include response bodies, Authorization, or sensitive URLs in newly added diagnostic messages.

## Outcome

The skeleton's production container topology is a decided architecture, not an inherited default — and whatever is chosen matches the serving story the rest of the skeleton documents.

## Problem

`skeleton/Dockerfile` builds on `php:8.5-fpm-alpine` and ends with `EXPOSE 9000`. That image speaks FastCGI: it answers nothing on its own, and the skeleton ships no web-server configuration to put in front of it.

Everything else in the skeleton assumes FrankenPHP:

- `composer run dev` routes to `waaseyaa/frankenphp`'s `dev` command.
- `README.md` §"Serving with FrankenPHP" is the documented serving path, including worker mode.
- `config/frankenphp/Caddyfile` and `config/frankenphp/php.ini` are committed.
- `skeleton/public/index.php` is a three-runtime adapter whose worker-mode branch keys off `WAASEYAA_FRANKENPHP_WORKER`, set by that committed Caddyfile.
- `waaseyaa/frankenphp` is installed by default.

So a consumer following the documentation locally, then building the shipped Dockerfile, gets a production image that does not serve and whose runtime differs from everything they tested against.

Surfaced while repairing #2673 (PR #2698). Deliberately **not** changed there: repairing a build that never worked is a bug fix; changing what the image serves is a deployment-contract migration, and it must not ride along with one.

## Scope — compare two options, do not assume the answer

**A. Keep FPM, backward compatible.** Consumers already running the FPM image behind their own nginx or Caddy keep working. Requires deciding what the skeleton owes them: a documented reference front-end config, or an explicit statement that the front end is consumer-owned.

**B. FrankenPHP default, self-serving.** `dunglas/frankenphp`, `EXPOSE 80 443`, reusing the committed Caddyfile — production matches the runtime the docs, the dev command, and the SSE/worker story already assume. Breaks anyone running the current image behind their own front end.

Either way, decide and record:

- **Ports** — `9000` FastCGI versus `80`/`443`, and what that implies for orchestration and health probing.
- **Caddyfile ownership** — is `config/frankenphp/Caddyfile` framework-owned, consumer-owned, or a scaffold the consumer adopts? It is currently committed to the skeleton and read by worker mode.
- **Health checks** — the image has none today. `Waaseyaa\Foundation\Diagnostic\CleanUrlProbe` and the `waaseyaa.clean_url_probe` route already exist and are the natural probe target.
- **Worker mode** — classic per-request or the warm worker the README calls "best for heavy SSE"? `public/index.php` supports both and refuses to infer the mode, so this must be an explicit deployment decision.
- **Upgrade guidance** — if B, what an existing FPM consumer does; a `docs/upgrade-notes/` entry is the established shape.

## Acceptance

- The decision and its rejected alternative are recorded, with the reason (an ADR if the deployment contract changes).
- The shipped image serves a request end to end in CI, or the front end is explicitly documented as consumer-owned with a reference configuration.
- A health check exists, or its absence is a recorded decision.
- If the contract changes, upgrade guidance ships with it.
- `bin/check-skeleton-docker-secret-exclusion` and the #2673 production-image step both stay green.

## Notes

- Do not fold this into #2673. That PR must remain a build repair.
- `skeleton/public/index.php` is byte-locked to `skeleton/bin/maintenance/golden-public-index.php` by `waaseyaa-audit-site`; if the topology change touches the front controller, both move together.
- Related: #2673 / PR #2698, #2647. Raised during the 2026-08-29 skeleton work.

## Outcome

Local/testing auth flows without a configured mail transport have a secure, intentional way to retrieve email-verification and password-reset actions. The mechanism must remain unavailable in production-equivalent environments and must not weaken global log redaction.

## Confirmed defect

`AuthConfig` selects `MailMissingPolicy::DevLog` in development/testing. Registration and recovery controllers log a URL containing the plaintext one-time token.

After #2694 composes the runtime logger correctly, a disposable real HTTP registration reaches the logger, but `RedactorProcessor` replaces the entire message with `[REDACTED]`. Before #2694 the message was silently lost to `NullLogger`; after it, the global security boundary correctly refuses to disclose the token. In both cases the advertised DevLog workflow is unusable: a local user cannot verify the newly registered account or complete password reset without a mail transport.

This is a contract conflict, not a request to exempt tokens from normal logs.

## Design constraints

- Do not allow verification/reset tokens into ordinary logs, structured context, traces, audit events, or error responses.
- Do not add a production flag that can accidentally expose tokens.
- Keep one-time token TTL, hashing, consumption, and revocation unchanged.
- The local delivery mechanism must be explicit, bounded, and unavailable in production-equivalent environments.
- Prefer a dedicated development outbox/sink with restrictive permissions or an equivalent typed interface over regex exemptions in the global redactor.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Registration, resend-verification, and forgot-password actions can be completed locally with no external mail service.
- [ ] The token/action is recoverable only through the explicit development delivery mechanism.
- [ ] Ordinary runtime logs continue to redact token-bearing URLs and token fields.
- [ ] Production/staging refuse the development mechanism at boot or do not bind it.
- [ ] Automated tests exercise registration → verification and forgot → reset through the real route composition boundary.
- [ ] Negative tests prove the mechanism is unavailable in production and does not leak through logs/responses.
- [ ] Auth documentation names the supported local workflow; `DevLog` is renamed/redefined if logs are no longer the transport.

## Priority rationale

`priority:p1`: this blocks the framework''s own mail-less local account lifecycle and reliable consumer E2E testing, but global redaction is currently failing safe rather than leaking credentials.

## Outcome

The file-level target guard in `bimaaji:install`'s sandbox has Windows execution evidence, or its absence is recorded as an explicit environmental limitation.

## Context — this is a proof gap, not a known defect

#2656 (PR #2683, merged as `aa0d70d2f`) added a layered containment boundary to `BimaajiInstallCommand::resolvePathInSandbox()`:

1. textual — empty, absolute, or `..`
2. **ancestor** — the nearest existing ancestor must resolve inside the project root
3. **target** — the target path itself must not be a link, and an existing target must resolve inside the project root

Layer 3 exists because `is_link()` does not report a Windows directory junction, so the guard resolves the target with `realpath()` rather than trusting `is_link()`.

`bin/check-bimaaji-junction-containment.ps1`, running in `ci/skeleton-create-project-windows`, now proves the platform premise on a real Windows runner: PHP `realpath()` follows a junction outside the project, an unguarded write escapes through it, and both the manifest and `.claude/skills` cases are contained with external SHA256 sentinels and non-zero exits.

What that proof **cannot** cover: a Windows directory junction is directory-only, so it exercises layer 2, not layer 3. The file-level case needs a Windows **file symbolic link**, which normally requires `SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege` or Developer Mode — the exact privilege requirement junctions were chosen to avoid.

So layer 3 is proven on Linux (six sentinel tests in `InstallCommandSandboxContainmentTest`) and reasoned-but-unexecuted on Windows. No containment defect is known or suspected; this closes an evidence gap.

## Acceptance

- Determine whether the hosted `windows-2025` runner can create a **file** symbolic link (Developer Mode state, or the runner account holding `SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege`). Record the finding with the evidence.
- **If it can:** execute the write, prune, and neutralisation sentinel cases against a file symlink on that runner, asserting external sentinel bytes unchanged — the same standard as the Linux cases and the junction gate. Assert the link was created rather than skipping when it cannot be.
- **If it cannot:** record the environmental limitation explicitly — in the guard's docblock and the containment section of `docs/specs/bimaaji-install.md` — stating what is proven where and why the Windows file-symlink case is unexecutable on the hosted runner. Do **not** add a vacuous skip that reports success without testing anything; `bin/check-phpunit-skip-policy` and `docs/specs/phpunit-skip-governance.md` govern any skip that is introduced.

## Notes

- Do not weaken `ci/skeleton-create-project-windows`'s contract to fit this. That lane is PowerShell and PHP by construction and runs no PHPUnit suites.
- Related: #2656 / PR #2683, parent #2653. Found during the 2026-08-29 review of that PR.

## Outcome

Multiple client transformers can write to a shared agent-context file without one client's pruning removing another's contribution.

## Problem

#2656 (PR #2683) corrects the Codex transformer's target from `.codex/AGENTS.md` — which is the personal `$CODEX_HOME` scope, not project scope — to the repository-root `AGENTS.md`. That correction is right. It also creates a boundary this design does not yet handle.

Root `AGENTS.md` is a **multi-writer path**. Codex reads it as its project contract; Junie's preferred location is `.junie/AGENTS.md` with root as a fallback; Devin Desktop reads it too; and it is a file users routinely hand-author. #2683's marker-bounded splice protects hand-authored content *outside* the managed region, and its `.waaseyaa/bimaaji-install.json` manifest records what Bimaaji generated. Neither mechanism handles two *managed* clients claiming the same path.

Concretely: if two transformers are ever configured to target root `AGENTS.md`, the manifest records the path once per client with a single sha1 of the bytes on disk. A later run that retires one client's skill set can then prune or neutralise a region the other client still owns — the manifest cannot distinguish whose contribution the bytes represent.

Today only Codex targets root `AGENTS.md`, so this is latent, not live. It becomes live the moment a second transformer is pointed there — which is a plausible next step, since Junie's own documentation names root `AGENTS.md` as a valid location.

## Scope

- Decide whether a shared path may carry more than one managed region, or whether one client owns it exclusively.
- If shared: managed regions need per-client identity, and the manifest needs per-client ownership within a single file rather than per-path.
- If exclusive: the install command must refuse or diagnose a second client claiming an already-claimed shared path, rather than silently interleaving.
- Either way, pruning and neutralisation must never remove a region belonging to a client other than the one being retired.

## Acceptance

- The chosen model is recorded, with the reason.
- A positive control proves that retiring one client's skills leaves another client's managed region in the same file byte-identical.
- The behaviour is the same on the `ci/skeleton-create-project-windows` lane as on Linux.

## Notes

- Related: #2656 / PR #2683 (the manifest, marker-bounded splice, and the Codex path correction), parent #2653.
- The three legacy-but-still-read targets recorded in the "Convention drift" section of the bimaaji-install spec — Cursor, Windsurf, Junie — each need their own decision and are not covered here.
- Found during the 2026-08-29 review of PR #2683.

## Summary

`EntityStorageDriverInterface::write($entityType, $id, $values)` takes the row's identity twice: once as the authoritative `$id` argument, and again — implicitly — as whatever `$values` carries under the entity type's id key. No first-party driver reconciles the two, and the three behaviours diverge from each other.

Raised in review of #2668 (fix for #2646). That PR narrowed the *documentation* to describe what the drivers actually do; this issue tracks making them agree.

## Measured behaviour

Writing `['id' => '99', 'title' => 'x']` while addressing `$id = '7'`:

| Case | `SqlStorageDriver` | `InMemoryStorageDriver` |
|---|---|---|
| INSERT (fresh row) | returns `'7'`, persists `id=99` → **`read('7')` is `null`** | returns `'7'`, persists `id=99` at store key `'7'` (still readable) |
| UPDATE (row seeded) | drops the divergent id, `id` stays `'7'` | returns `'7'`, persists `id=99` |

The SQL INSERT case is the worst of the three: `write()` returns an id at which the row it just wrote **cannot be read back**. `EntityRepository` would then hold an id that addresses nothing.

Repro script: see the verification in #2668 (`SqlStorageDriver` + `InMemoryStorageDriver` side by side against a SQLite `varchar` id table).

## Why it hasn't bitten

Not reachable through `EntityRepository` today: `writeDriverRow()` derives `$id` and the value bag from the same entity, so they cannot disagree, and mutating identity on a live entity is refused (`LogicException: Structural field <type>.<id> is immutable after construction`). It is reachable from direct fixture writes and from any third-party driver consumer.

`SqlStorageDriver`'s UPDATE branch already documents the intended rule (`SqlStorageDriver.php:230-245`): *"row identity is immutable through the storage driver... A divergent id value in `$values` is silently dropped"*, pinned by `SqlStorageDriverTest::updateNeverRewritesTheIdColumn`. The INSERT branch simply does not apply it.

## Proposed direction

Apply the existing UPDATE rule uniformly: `$id`, when non-empty, is authoritative on **both** branches, and a divergent bag id is dropped rather than persisted. Then pin it in `AbstractEntityStorageDriverContract` so every implementation inherits the guarantee — the same mechanism #2668 used for the auto-assigned-id round trip.

Worth deciding explicitly whether a divergent id should be *dropped silently* (matching today's UPDATE contract) or *rejected loudly*, since silently discarding caller data has its own failure mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- `write($type, $id, $values)` with a non-empty `$id` persists a row readable at `$id` on every first-party driver, regardless of what `$values` carries under the id key.
- The INSERT-returns-an-unreadable-id case above is impossible.
- `AbstractEntityStorageDriverContract` covers divergent-id writes on both the insert and update paths, so both drivers are gated.
- The narrowed contract text in `EntityStorageDriverInterface::write()` and `docs/specs/entity-system.md` is updated to state the stronger guarantee once it holds.
