## Current backlog disposition (2026-08-16)

**Measurable outcome:** Define the smallest turnkey RAG contract that preserves passage text, source identity, chunk provenance, and provider wiring.

**Dependencies / links:** Builds on the shipped embedding CLI and current ai-vector store.

**Why this is not ready:** No canonical document model, source-text custody rule, or repeated consumer requirement is recorded.

**Authority boundary:** This disposition preserves the idea; it does not authorize implementation, release, deployment, production activation, or operational mutation.

---

## Original report (preserved)

Three coupled gaps mean vector RAG **cannot work by just installing the package** — each had to be solved app-side.

**1. No service provider (note #010).** `ai-agent` / `ai-tools` / `ai-observability` / `ai-pipeline` each declare `extra.waaseyaa.providers` and auto-boot. **`ai-vector` and `ai-schema` declare none**, so installing ai-vector wires nothing: `EntityEmbeddingListener` is not subscribed, no `EmbeddingStorageInterface` / `EmbeddingProviderInterface` is bound, and the `embeddings` table is never created. The package looks "installed and ready" but is inert.

**2. Vector-only store + entity-driven embedding (note #011).** `EmbeddingStorageInterface::store(entityType, id, vector)` persists only the float vector keyed by `(entity_type, entity_id)`; `findSimilar()` returns `{id, score}`. No source text is stored, so grounding a model requires the app to keep chunk text elsewhere and join on the returned id. Embedding is entity-driven (`EntityEmbeddingListener` on `EntityEvent::POST_SAVE`), so non-entity content (Twig pages) can't be embedded without first synthesizing entity/chunk records.

**3. No embed CLI / handler (note #014).** `SemanticIndexWarmer` (batch embed) has no `bin/waaseyaa` command, and `EntityEmbeddingListener` can dispatch `GenericMessage(type: 'ai_vector.embed_entity')` for which **no handler ships**. There is no out-of-the-box way to (re)build embeddings.

**Where it bit us (oiatc-waaseyaa, alpha.188)**

To do grounded retrieval we wrote our own service provider (bind storage + provider, subscribe the listener), introduced a `doc_chunk` table holding `{source_url, title, text}`, and hand-warmed the index. Ultimately we shipped a keyword retrieve-then-prompt (Path B) controller because vector RAG wasn't turnkey.

**Suggested fix**

- Ship an `AiVectorServiceProvider` (declared in `ai-vector/composer.json` `extra.waaseyaa.providers`) that wires storage + provider + listeners from the existing `ai.embedding_provider` config, no-opping cleanly when the provider is empty — matching how the other ai-* packages self-wire.
- Offer a first-class "passage/chunk" source (text + metadata + vector in one record) and a non-entity ingestion path, plus optional text-chunking.
- Ship a `bin/waaseyaa ai:embed[:warm]` command and a default handler for the `ai_vector.embed_entity` message, so populating the index is a documented one-liner.

---
*Field report from building [oiatc-waaseyaa](https://github.com/waaseyaa/oiatc-waaseyaa) on alpha.188. Source: `docs/waaseyaa-upstream-notes.md` #010, #011, #014.*

## Current backlog disposition (2026-08-16)

**Measurable outcome:** Specify a non-oracular JSON:API signal that distinguishes policy-filtered empty collections from genuinely empty data.

**Dependencies / links:** Depends on collection access policy, caching, and error-envelope compatibility.

**Why this is not ready:** The wire status/envelope semantics and leakage analysis require a decision first.

**Authority boundary:** This disposition preserves the idea; it does not authorize implementation, release, deployment, production activation, or operational mutation.

---

## Original report (preserved)

**Symptom**

With no `AccessPolicy` registered for an entity type, `EntityAccessHandler::check($entity, 'view', $account)` aggregates to `Neutral`. For the **single-entity GET** that yields a clear `403`, but for the **collection GET** (`/api/{type}`) the controller filters each row by `isAllowed()` (`JsonApiController:~85`) and returns **`200` with `data: []`** — an empty list, no error, no warning. A freshly registered content type therefore looks *"publicly readable but empty"* rather than *"not yet authorized,"* which reads as a data bug, not an access decision.

**Where it bit us (oiatc-waaseyaa, alpha.188)**

During the AI-layer audit, `/api/news_post` (a new entity with no policy) read as "open but empty," which looked like a data bug until we added an explicit `NewsPostAccessPolicy` (published rows public, drafts gated).

**Suggested fix**

Fail-closed is the right default, but the **silent** empty collection is a footgun. Options:
- (a) when a list is filtered down by access, include a JSON:API `meta` note or emit a `debug`-level log ("N rows hidden by access policy");
- (b) document prominently that a new content entity needs a view-granting policy to be API-readable;
- (c) optionally surface a boot-time/dev-mode notice when a registered entity type has no policy at all.

Any of these turns a confusing empty list into an obvious "you haven't authorized this yet."

---
*Field report from building [oiatc-waaseyaa](https://github.com/waaseyaa/oiatc-waaseyaa) on alpha.188. Source: `docs/waaseyaa-upstream-notes.md` #009.*

## Current status / retirement ledger (2026-08-16)

Current main still contains `packages/database-legacy`, and 32 sibling package manifests still mention `waaseyaa/database-legacy` across runtime and development requirements. Deletion remains prohibited until every dependency is classified and migrated. This issue is a retirement ledger, not one implementation PR.

### Child work checklist

- [ ] Inventory every current manifest reference as runtime, development-only, replacement/provide, or stale.
- [ ] Approve the destination and compatibility contract for the `Waaseyaa\Database` namespace.
- [ ] Create/link bounded child issues by dependency cohort; each child must migrate its consumers and keep `composer install` plus canonical gates green.
- [ ] Migrate runtime consumers before development-only/test consumers.
- [ ] Add a repository guard proving no path-repository package can be deleted while a manifest still requires it.
- [ ] Only after all child migrations land, create a separately reviewed deletion issue for package/path-repo/autoload cleanup.

### Exit criteria

- No package manifest requires `waaseyaa/database-legacy`.
- The replacement API/namespace is documented and consumer compatibility tests are green.
- Composer install, package-boundary checks, PHPStan, unit/integration tests, and split-package checks pass from a clean checkout.
- The final deletion is independently reviewed and leaves no split/Packagist/consumer reference behind.

### Authority guard

This ledger does not authorize package deletion, release, split publication, downstream consumer mutation, deployment, or production data migration. Those require separately scoped and reviewed work.

---

## Original report (preserved)
## Why this exists  The `database-legacy-retirement-01KSEFV2` mission was merged and then **reverted** (`2b4db713e`, "Revert ...lane-a squash-merge") during post-merge triage on 2026-05-28 because it was incomplete and broke CI for the entire repo — `composer install` failed everywhere with:  > `Source path "packages/database-legacy" is not found for package waaseyaa/database-legacy`  ## Root cause  The mission deleted the `packages/database-legacy/` directory and removed it from `composer.json`, but **19 packages still `require waaseyaa/database-legacy`** (mostly runtime, some `require-dev`), and the `Waaseyaa\Database` namespace code was **not relocated** to any other package. So consumers' dependency requirements pointed at a missing path repo.  Consumers requiring `waaseyaa/database-legacy` (runtime where verified): - `packages/entity-storage/composer.json` — runtime - `packages/audit/composer.json` — runtime - `packages/migration/composer.json` — runtime - `packages/api/composer.json` — require-dev - …and ~15 others (full list via `grep -rln 'database-legacy' --include=composer.json packages/`)  ## Acceptance criteria for re-attempt  - [ ] Identify a target package for the `Waaseyaa\Database` namespace (or fully replace its API surface with another DB abstraction). - [ ] **Migrate every consumer** off `waaseyaa/database-legacy` to the new location/API — each in its own commit per package, validated by CI. - [ ] Only then delete `packages/database-legacy/` and remove the path-repo entry + the autoload-dev `Waaseyaa\Database\Tests\` line from the root `composer.json`. - [ ] CI must stay green at each step (no commit that breaks `composer install`). - [ ] Review explicitly verifies "all 19 consumers migrated" rather than passing on the mission-package's tests alone.  ## Lesson from this revert  A mission that deletes a path-repo'd package must include consumer migration as part of its work-package scope; reviewing only the mission's own tests will not catch dangling `require` entries. Add a CI check that fails fast on any `Source path ... not found` error from `composer install`.  🤖 Filed by Claude Opus 4.7 during post-merge triage (session HEAD `d58ab5349`).
